In the account of Canaan House that runs alongside the present-day chapters of this book, he did not leave: he is Harrowhark's cavalier primary throughout, a mournful, unathletic man still reciting his unfinished epic poem, and Gideon Nav is not there at all.
characters.name: Ortus Nigenad

characters.description: A Resurrection Beast: the accumulated ghost of a world that died when the old system did, grown over ten thousand years into something enormous, and one of a small number of them that hunt the Emperor across space. Number Seven is on its way to the Lyctors' station, and killing it is the reason the new Lyctors are being trained at all.
characters.name: Number Seven

characters.description: Necromancer heir of the Fifth House, a historian whose art is speaking with ghosts and with the distant past. She appears in this book's account of the events at Canaan House, where she is the candidate most interested in what the First House was before it was abandoned, and the one most willing to organize the others.
characters.name: Abigail Pent

characters.description: A figure lying in a sealed coffin in the depths of Canaan House in this book's account of it, dressed in clothing from nowhere in the Nine Houses and carrying a weapon nobody there recognises. She is not dead. As the account proceeds she begins to wake, and what she is interested in is Harrowhark.
characters.name: The Sleeper

recaps.ending: Harrowhark's condition turns out to be self-inflicted. Before leaving Canaan House she had Ianthe perform surgery on her brain to cut Gideon Nav out of her memory entirely, so that she could never consume her. That is why she is an immortal Lyctor with none of a Lyctor's power, Gideon's soul sitting intact and untouched inside her, and why the Canaan House she remembers has Ortus Nigenad in it instead. When that arrangement collapses, Gideon wakes in Harrowhark's body and narrates the rest of the book. Mercymorn and Augustine choose the same moment to make the attempt on the Emperor they have been preparing for ten thousand years, telling Gideon first what he actually did: the Resurrection Beasts are the ghosts of the worlds he himself destroyed, and the Empire is built on that. The attempt fails, the Emperor survives it, Mercymorn does not, and the station is destroyed in the process. The body of the Saint of Duty proves to be shared with his own long-dead cavalier, Pyrrha Dve, who is still inside it. Gideon escapes aboard a shuttle with Ianthe, wearing Harrowhark's body and using Harrowhark's necromancy, while Harrowhark's own soul is left adrift in the River inside the wreck of the Canaan House her surgery built. Harrowhark is lost, the Empire's founding crime is known to the people who survived, and Gideon leaves the book intending to get her back.
recaps.in_short: Harrowhark Nonagesimus leaves Canaan House as one of the Emperor's Lyctors and is taken to his station beyond the Nine Houses to be trained against the Resurrection Beasts, the vast ghosts of dead worlds that hunt him. She is a disaster: constantly ill, unable to use a Lyctor's power, unsure of her own perceptions, and under repeated attack by one of the Emperor's ancient saints. Interleaved with this is an account of the events of the previous book in which Gideon Nav does not exist, Harrowhark's cavalier is Ortus Nigenad, and a sleeping woman in a coffin wakes and hunts her. The two are the same problem: before leaving the First House, Harrowhark had Ianthe cut Gideon out of her memory so that she could never consume her, leaving Gideon's soul intact inside her and Harrowhark a Lyctor in name only. When the arrangement fails, Gideon wakes in Harrowhark's body. Mercymorn and Augustine make their long-planned attempt to kill the Emperor, revealing that he destroyed the old worlds himself; the attempt fails and the station is destroyed with it. Gideon escapes with Ianthe, wearing Harrowhark's body, while Harrowhark's soul is left adrift in the River.

recaps.text: Previously, in Gideon the Ninth: the Emperor summoned the necromantic heir and cavalier of each of the Nine Houses to Canaan House, the abandoned seat of the First House, to compete for elevation to Lyctor, the immortal saints who serve him. Harrowhark Nonagesimus, heir of the Ninth House, went with Gideon Nav, an indentured servant of the Ninth and her lifelong enemy, who stood in as her cavalier in exchange for her freedom. The candidates were given no instructions, only a sealed facility of laboratories beneath the house, and then they began to be murdered. The secret of Lyctorhood proved to be that a necromancer becomes immortal by consuming their own cavalier's soul, which then powers them forever. Ianthe Tridentarius of the Third House killed her cavalier to claim it. The Seventh House's dying heir was revealed to be Cytherea the First, one of the Emperor's original Lyctors, who had been killing the candidates; Palamedes Sextus of the Sixth destroyed himself trying to stop her, and most of the others died. Rather than let Harrowhark be killed refusing the price, Gideon impaled herself on an iron railing so that Harrow would have no choice. Harrowhark ascended, destroyed Cytherea, and was taken off the First House alive: a Lyctor, with Gideon's soul inside her, and unwilling to accept it.

The book runs on two tracks. In the present, Harrowhark has been taken far beyond the Nine Houses to the Emperor's station, where the new Lyctors are to be trained, and she is plainly broken: she vomits blood, she cannot do what a Lyctor is supposed to do, her perception of her own surroundings cannot be relied upon, and she is convinced that someone aboard means to kill her. Ianthe Tridentarius, who ascended without difficulty, is her only companion and not a kind one. Running alongside this is an account of the events at Canaan House from the previous book, told differently: in it Harrowhark's cavalier is Ortus Nigenad, who never fled the Ninth, and Gideon Nav does not exist at all. The two versions cannot both be true, and the Harrowhark of the present-day chapters gives no sign of noticing the difference.

The Emperor's station holds him and the three of his original Lyctors still alive: Mercymorn the First, hostile to Harrowhark from the moment she arrives; Augustine the First, merely amused by her; and the Saint of Duty, who says almost nothing to anyone. The Emperor himself is disarmingly ordinary and takes charge of Harrowhark's education personally. The purpose of the training is a Resurrection Beast, the ghost of a world that died ten thousand years ago and has been growing ever since, which is closing on the station and which the Lyctors will eventually have to go out and fight. Harrowhark is attacked, repeatedly and without explanation, by the Saint of Duty, and survives largely because she prepared for exactly that. She is also working from a numbered sequence of letters she wrote to herself in advance, each sealed and each to be opened only under a stated condition. Everywhere she goes she is accompanied by the Body, the corpse from the Ninth House's sealed tomb, whom nobody else can see. Meanwhile the Canaan House account continues, with Ortus at her side and the same candidates gathering for the same trials.

Harrowhark's training goes badly. Her body rebels, her necromancy behaves like a Ninth House adept's rather than a Lyctor's, and the ancients treat her as either an embarrassment or a threat. Mercymorn's hostility becomes explicit, Augustine keeps a polite distance, and the attempts on Harrowhark's life continue. Ianthe alternates between teaching her and using her, and the two settle into a partnership neither would call friendship. Harrowhark is taught what the River is, the medium the dead pass into and the thing necromancy actually draws on, and what it does to a soul that enters it unprotected. In the Canaan House account, the trials proceed and the candidates start dying much as before, and something new surfaces: deep in the facility there is a sealed coffin with a living woman inside it, dressed and armed like nothing in the Nine Houses. She is beginning to wake.

The attempts on Harrowhark's life escalate and she sets out to establish who is behind them and why, with her sealed letters as her only reliable source of instruction: each is opened at its stated moment, and each was written by someone who knew far more about her situation than she does. Ianthe extracts a price for every piece of help. In the Canaan House account the sleeper gets out of her coffin and begins hunting Harrowhark through the house while the surviving candidates try to hold her off. The two accounts begin interfering with each other, images and people from one appearing in the other, and Harrowhark's grip on which of them she is actually living in weakens. It becomes clear that her illness, her blind spots and the impossible version of Canaan House are all the same problem.

Both threads come apart. The Resurrection Beast reaches the system and the Lyctors have to meet it in the River, where the Beast and the ordinary dead can both reach a soul that is not properly defended, and Harrowhark, who cannot do what the others do, is a liability in a fight none of them can afford to lose. In the Canaan House account the sleeper runs the survivors down one by one and the house itself starts to fail, until the version of events Harrowhark has been living inside can no longer hold its shape. Her body gives out, and the thing she has been unable to reach since the moment she ascended, the reason she is a Lyctor with no Lyctor's power, finally forces its way to the surface.

The explanation is Harrowhark's own doing. Before leaving Canaan House she had Ianthe operate on her brain and cut Gideon Nav out of her memory entirely, precisely so that she could never use her. Gideon's soul is inside her, intact and unconsumed, which is why she has a Lyctor's immortality and none of a Lyctor's power, and the Canaan House she has been remembering is the version her mutilated memory could support, with Ortus Nigenad standing where Gideon should be. The sealed letters were left by the woman who planned all of it. With Harrowhark's own soul displaced into the River, Gideon wakes up in Harrowhark's body and takes over the narration of the book, with Harrowhark's necromancy at her disposal, Ianthe as her only ally, and everyone aboard the station having to decide what to do about a Lyctor who is suddenly somebody else.

With Gideon in control of Harrowhark's body, the situation on the station collapses. Mercymorn and Augustine reveal that they have spent ten thousand years waiting for a chance to kill the Emperor, and they tell the truth about the Resurrection first: the Resurrection Beasts are the ghosts of the worlds of the old system, and it was the Emperor who killed them. Their attempt fails. The Emperor survives it and Mercymorn does not, and the station is destroyed in the fighting. Gideon faces the Saint of Duty and finds that his body is shared with his own long-dead cavalier, Pyrrha Dve, who has been surfacing in it all along. Gideon and Ianthe get off the station alive aboard a shuttle. Harrowhark's soul is not with them: it is adrift in the River, inside the ruin of the imaginary Canaan House her surgery built, and recovering her is what Gideon leaves the book intending to do.

characters.description: Now twelve and heading into his second year at Hogwarts, Harry spends a miserable summer with the Dursleys, cut off from his friends and the wizarding world. Famous among wizards for surviving Voldemort as a baby, he is still an outsider at home. He is desperate to return to school, the first place he has ever belonged.
characters.name: Harry Potter

characters.description: Harry's loyal best friend, who rescues him from the Dursleys' house in his father's flying car along with his older twin brothers. One of many children in the warm, cheerfully chaotic Weasley family, he is still touchy about being poor but steadfast whenever Harry is in trouble.
characters.name: Ron Weasley

characters.description: Harry and Ron's studious, quick-thinking friend, born to non-magical parents. Her wide reading and careful planning repeatedly steer the trio, and this year her research proves central to uncovering what is stalking the school. She feels the sting of prejudice against Muggle-borns more sharply than before.
characters.name: Hermione Granger

characters.description: The youngest Weasley and the family's only girl, beginning her first year at Hogwarts. Shy and easily flustered around Harry, on whom she plainly has a crush, she is otherwise easily overlooked among her loud older brothers.
characters.name: Ginny Weasley

characters.description: A house-elf bound to serve a wizarding family, who appears uninvited in Harry's bedroom to warn him not to return to Hogwarts, insisting a deadly plot threatens him there. Small, big-eyed, and painfully devoted, he punishes himself whenever he criticizes his masters, and he is willing to endanger Harry in his clumsy efforts to save his life.
characters.name: Dobby

characters.description: A famous, self-adoring author of best-selling books about his supposed adventures fighting dark creatures, newly hired to teach Defence Against the Dark Arts. Beaming, handsome, and endlessly self-promoting, he turns every lesson into an advertisement for himself and proves far more interested in fame than in teaching.
characters.name: Gilderoy Lockhart

characters.description: Draco's father, a cold, wealthy, and influential wizard who moves easily among the powerful. Openly contemptuous of Muggle-borns and of the Weasleys, he carries himself with disdain and clearly holds sway over the school's board of governors.
characters.name: Lucius Malfoy

characters.description: Harry's sneering rival, more spiteful this year as attacks on Muggle-born students begin. He taunts Hermione with a slur for her parentage and openly hopes the school's hidden danger will target students like her, though he seems to know little of what is really behind it.
characters.name: Draco Malfoy

characters.description: The Hogwarts gamekeeper and Harry's steadfast friend, as fond as ever of dangerous creatures. As fear spreads through the school, old suspicion resurfaces about a scandal from his own student days, and he becomes an early target when the authorities look for someone to blame.
characters.name: Rubeus Hagrid

characters.description: The Hogwarts headmaster, calm and watchful as attacks on students throw the school into fear. He alone seems unafraid of the danger and continues to trust Harry, but pressure from the governors threatens his position as the crisis deepens.
characters.name: Albus Dumbledore

characters.description: A memory of a Hogwarts student from fifty years earlier, preserved inside an enchanted diary that writes back to whoever confides in it. Polite and helpful in tone, he offers to show Harry the truth about the last time the school's hidden chamber was opened, and the deaths that followed.
characters.name: Tom Riddle

recaps.ending: Harry reaches the Chamber of Secrets and finds Ginny Weasley near death, her life being drained into an enchanted diary. The diary preserved a memory of Tom Riddle, a former Hogwarts student who grew up to become Lord Voldemort; he had used the book to possess Ginny and reopen the Chamber, setting a giant basilisk to attack Muggle-born students. With help from Dumbledore's phoenix, Fawkes, and a sword produced by the Sorting Hat, Harry kills the basilisk, though its fang pierces him; Fawkes's tears heal the wound. Harry stabs the diary with the fang, destroying Riddle's memory and saving Ginny. It emerges that Lucius Malfoy had slipped the diary among Ginny's things to discredit the Weasleys and Dumbledore. Harry tricks Lucius into freeing his mistreated house-elf, Dobby, who is now devoted to Harry. The Petrified students are cured, Hagrid is cleared and released, and Dumbledore is restored as headmaster. Harry ends the year having faced Voldemort's past self and won, though the encounter has left him uneasy about how alike the two of them can seem.
recaps.in_short: In his second year, Harry is warned by a house-elf, Dobby, to stay away from Hogwarts, then finds the school terrorized by an unknown monster. A message on a wall announces that the Chamber of Secrets has been opened, and students begin turning up Petrified, all of them of non-magical descent. Harry discovers he can speak to snakes, which turns suspicion on him, and the school fears he is the culprit. Following the trail through an enchanted diary that shows a false memory, and past spiders and clues, Harry and Ron learn the monster is a giant serpent, a basilisk, moving through the castle's pipes, and that Ron's sister Ginny has been taken into the Chamber. Harry descends alone, confronts a memory of the young Tom Riddle, who is revealed to be Voldemort's teenage self, kills the basilisk with a sword, and destroys the diary, saving Ginny. Dobby is freed and Voldemort's plan through the diary is undone.

recaps.text: Harry Potter is an orphan who was raised by his cruel aunt and uncle, the Dursleys, and learned at eleven that he is a wizard, famous for surviving the attack in which the dark wizard Lord Voldemort killed his parents. At Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry he was sorted into Gryffindor House and made his first true friends, the loyal Ron Weasley and the brilliant, bookish Hermione Granger. In his first year he uncovered a plot to steal the Philosopher's Stone, a source of immortality, and found that the timid teacher Quirrell had been sheltering the weakened, bodiless Voldemort. Harry stopped the theft, protected by the sacrifice his mother made in dying for him, and the Stone was destroyed. Voldemort survived, powerless and in hiding, and Dumbledore, the school's headmaster, warned that he would one day try to return.

Harry endures a wretched summer with the Dursleys until a house-elf named Dobby appears in his bedroom and begs him not to return to Hogwarts, warning of a deadly plot; when Harry refuses, Dobby sabotages him to try to force him home, nearly getting him expelled. Ron and his twin brothers rescue Harry in their father's enchanted flying car and take him to the Weasleys' ramshackle home, the Burrow. On the crowded shopping trip to Diagon Alley, Harry meets the vain celebrity author Gilderoy Lockhart, the new Defence teacher, and clashes with Draco Malfoy and his cold, sneering father, Lucius, who despises the Weasleys and everything they stand for. When the boys are unable to reach the hidden platform to catch the school train, they take the flying car to Hogwarts instead, crashing it spectacularly and drawing the fury of the Potions master, Snape.

Settling into a second year of lessons made ridiculous by Lockhart's showing off, Harry begins to hear a cold, murderous voice moving through the castle walls that no one else can hear. On Halloween the caretaker's cat is found Petrified beneath a message daubed on the wall: the Chamber of Secrets has been opened, and its enemies should beware. According to legend the Chamber was built centuries earlier by one of the school's founders, Salazar Slytherin, who wanted to purge Hogwarts of students without pure wizarding blood, and it hides a monster only his heir can control. Suspicion and fear spread through the school. Harry, Ron, and Hermione begin to investigate, and their attention drifts toward Draco Malfoy as a likely heir, though they have no proof.

The attacks continue and more students, all of non-magical descent, are found Petrified. At a duelling club Harry accidentally reveals that he can speak to snakes, a rare ability strongly associated with Slytherin and dark magic, and the school turns against him, many now convinced he is the heir opening the Chamber. Hoping to catch the culprit, the trio brew a difficult potion to disguise Ron and Harry as Draco's friends and question him, only to learn he knows nothing about who is behind the attacks. Meanwhile Harry finds an old, blank diary that once belonged to a student named Tom Riddle. When Harry writes in it, Riddle writes back and shows him a memory in which, fifty years earlier, Riddle accused the boy Hagrid of opening the Chamber and keeping a dangerous creature, getting him expelled.

The diary is stolen from Harry's dormitory, and soon afterward Hermione is Petrified. Before she was struck she left the trio a vital clue: the monster in the Chamber is a basilisk, a giant serpent whose direct gaze kills and whose reflected or indirect gaze only Petrifies, and it has been travelling unseen through the castle's plumbing. That explains why no victim has died and why Harry alone could hear it, since he can understand snakes. With the school on the edge of closing, Ginny Weasley is taken down into the Chamber itself, and a new message warns that she will die there. Harry and Ron force the reluctant Lockhart to come with them and find the entrance in a girls' bathroom, opening it with the snake-speech Harry did not know he was using.

In the tunnels Lockhart tries to flee and wipe the boys' memories, but his stolen wand backfires and erases his own, and a cave-in separates Harry from Ron. Harry goes on alone and finds Ginny unconscious, her life draining away, watched over by the memory of Tom Riddle, who has stepped out of the diary. Riddle reveals that he is the young Lord Voldemort, that he framed Hagrid years ago, and that he has used the diary to possess Ginny and reopen the Chamber. He sets the basilisk on Harry. Fawkes, Dumbledore's phoenix, blinds the serpent and brings Harry the Sorting Hat, from which Harry draws a sword and kills the basilisk, taking a fatal bite that Fawkes's tears then heal. Harry stabs the diary with a basilisk fang, destroying Riddle and reviving Ginny. Above ground, Lucius Malfoy is exposed as the one who planted the diary; Harry frees the Malfoys' house-elf, Dobby; the Petrified students are cured; and Hagrid is cleared and Dumbledore reinstated.

characters.description: The middle child of Harry and Ginny Potter, beginning his years at Hogwarts in the shadow of his famous father. Uneasy and self-doubting, he is sorted into Slytherin rather than Gryffindor, struggles to make friends beyond one, and comes to resent being the son of the celebrated Harry Potter. His prickly, wounded relationship with his father and his longing to matter drive much of the story.
characters.name: Albus Severus Potter

characters.description: The only son of Draco Malfoy, a kind, bookish, and lonely boy dogged by a cruel rumor about his parentage. Gentle and quick-witted, with a fondness for sweets and history, he becomes Albus Potter's devoted best friend from their first meeting on the Hogwarts Express and remains loyal through every danger that follows.
characters.name: Scorpius Malfoy

characters.description: Now a grown man, husband to Ginny and father of three, and a senior official at the Ministry of Magic in charge of magical law enforcement. Still marked by the traumas of his youth, he finds fatherhood harder than any battle and clashes painfully with his son Albus, unsure how to reach a boy who feels nothing like him. The old scar and old enemies are not as distant as he would like.
characters.name: Harry Potter

characters.description: Harry's wife and Albus's mother, working now as a sports editor at the Daily Prophet. Warm, level-headed, and quietly firm, she often mediates between her husband and their unhappy son, seeing both sides more clearly than either can.
characters.name: Ginny Potter

characters.description: Harry's oldest friend and Hermione's husband, who runs Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, the family joke shop. Good-humored and affectionate, he is the comic, easygoing uncle of the group, devoted to his family and quick with a joke even when things turn serious.
characters.name: Ron Weasley

characters.description: Harry's brilliant friend from his school years, now Minister for Magic and married to Ron. As capable and principled as ever, she carries the weight of governing the wizarding world, and a dangerous artifact recovered by the Ministry falls under her keeping.
characters.name: Hermione Granger

characters.description: Harry's old school rival, now a wealthy widower and the father of Scorpius. Cold and proud in public, he is fiercely protective of his son and stung by the rumors that surround the boy. His long antagonism with Harry lingers, though both are older and wearier now.
characters.name: Draco Malfoy

characters.description: The elderly, embittered father of Cedric Diggory, living in a wizarding care home and consumed by grief for the son he lost long ago. He confronts Harry with a furious demand: that the Ministry use a rumored Time-Turner to go back and save Cedric from death.
characters.name: Amos Diggory

characters.description: A striking young woman introduced as the niece and caretaker of the elderly Amos Diggory. Warm, confident, and encouraging toward Albus, she takes a keen interest in his wish to put right an old wrong and offers herself as a friend and helper to the boys' secret plan, presenting herself as an ally to their cause.
characters.name: Delphi

characters.description: A Hogwarts student of Harry's generation, a well-liked champion who was killed years earlier during the Triwizard Tournament. He does not appear in the present, but his death and his father's grief set the whole story in motion, and he becomes the target of a scheme to reach back and change the past.
characters.name: Cedric Diggory

characters.description: The long-dead former headmaster of Hogwarts, present now only as a portrait in the Ministry and at the school. His painted likeness counsels Harry on the burdens of the past and of fatherhood, though a portrait can offer only an echo of the man's wisdom.
characters.name: Albus Dumbledore

characters.description: The former Hogwarts professor, long dead in the world the boys know. He appears when their meddling with time conjures an altered reality, where he is alive and secretly working against a triumphant dark regime. Sardonic and brave, he aids Scorpius at great personal risk to help set the world right.
characters.name: Severus Snape

recaps.ending: Delphi is revealed as the hidden child of Voldemort and Bellatrix Lestrange, and her plan is to undo her father's defeat. After forcing Albus and Scorpius to help her travel back in time, she goes to Godric's Hollow on the night in 1981 when Voldemort came to kill the infant Harry, intending to stop the rebounding curse that destroyed him. The boys manage to summon Harry, Ginny, Ron, Hermione, and Draco to that night. Together they confront and overpower Delphi, and Harry endures the anguish of standing by while his own parents are killed so that history runs its true course and Voldemort is once again undone. Delphi is captured and imprisoned. In the aftermath, the long rift between Harry and Albus finally heals as father and son come to understand each other, and Harry's old enmity with Draco softens into something like respect. Scorpius and Albus remain fast friends, having saved their world by choosing, in the end, not to change the past. The dangerous Time-Turner and the temptation it represents are set aside, and the two families step into a steadier future.
recaps.in_short: Set nineteen years after the fall of Voldemort, the play follows Harry Potter's unhappy son Albus, who is sorted into Slytherin and befriends Scorpius Malfoy. Straining against his father's legend, Albus overhears the grieving Amos Diggory beg Harry to save Cedric with a Time-Turner, and, encouraged by Amos's niece Delphi, the boys steal the device and travel back to the Triwizard Tournament to prevent Cedric's death. Their meddling warps the present again and again, at its worst producing a nightmare world where Voldemort won and Harry is dead, which Scorpius barely undoes with help from a still-living Snape and others. Back in a restored present, Delphi reveals herself as the secret daughter of Voldemort and Bellatrix Lestrange, bent on resurrecting her father. She forces the boys through time and travels to Godric's Hollow on the night in 1981 when Voldemort first attacked the Potters, meaning to change history in his favor. Albus and Scorpius summon Harry and the others; together they defeat Delphi and let the true past unfold. Harry and Albus, and Harry and Draco, are reconciled by what they have survived.

recaps.text: Over seven earlier books, the orphaned wizard Harry Potter discovered he was famous in the magical world as the only person to survive the killing curse of the dark wizard Voldemort, who had murdered his parents. Across his years at Hogwarts School, Harry, with his friends Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger, repeatedly thwarted Voldemort's return to power. In their fourth year, Voldemort returned to a body and a schoolmate, Cedric Diggory, was killed. Harry learned that Voldemort had split his soul into hidden objects to make himself deathless, and with Ron and Hermione he hunted and destroyed them, culminating in the Battle of Hogwarts, where Voldemort was finally killed and the wizarding world freed. Nineteen years later, Harry has married Ginny Weasley and has children; Ron and Hermione have married and have a daughter; and Draco Malfoy, Harry's old school rival, has a son of his own. The war is history, but its wounds and its enemies have not entirely faded.

As the play opens, Harry and Ginny's son Albus is starting at Hogwarts, dreading life as the famous Harry Potter's child. On the train he befriends Scorpius Malfoy, a kind and lonely boy shadowed by a nasty rumor, and the two become inseparable. To Albus's dismay he is sorted into Slytherin and proves a mediocre student, and over the next few school years he grows more miserable and more estranged from his father, until the two can barely speak without wounding each other. The grieving Amos Diggory arrives to confront Harry, demanding that the Ministry use a rumored Time-Turner to go back and save his son Cedric, who died long ago; Harry refuses. Albus, overhearing, resolves to do what his father will not. He meets Amos's niece Delphi, who encourages him, and determines to steal the Time-Turner and undo Cedric's death, hoping at last to prove himself and do something that matters.

Albus and Scorpius run away from the Hogwarts Express and, with Delphi's help, get hold of the Ministry's confiscated Time-Turner. Believing that saving Cedric is the right thing to do, they travel back to the Triwizard Tournament to sabotage his performance in the first task, reasoning that if he never wins the tournament he will never reach the danger that killed him. But changing the past has consequences the boys do not foresee. When they return to the present, the world has shifted around them in unsettling ways, relationships and lives rearranged by their interference. Alarmed, they realize that meddling with time is far more dangerous than they imagined, and that fixing one grief has unraveled things they never meant to touch. Determined to put matters right, they resolve to use the Time-Turner again, not understanding how much worse their next attempt can make things.

The boys' second attempt to save Cedric goes catastrophically wrong. Their interference humiliates Cedric so deeply that, in the timeline it creates, he turns to Voldemort's side, and the ripple of that change produces a nightmare present: Voldemort won the war, Harry is dead, and a cruel regime rules the wizarding world. Scorpius, separated from Albus and finding himself alone in this dark reality, must navigate a Hogwarts run by fear, where a still-living Severus Snape, along with Ron and Hermione as hunted rebels, help him understand what has happened. Snape sacrifices himself so that Scorpius can act, and Scorpius manages to reverse the change and restore the proper world, reuniting with Albus. Shaken but grateful, the boys return to a present that is nearly right again, their meddling seemingly at an end, still trusting the friend who first urged them on and unaware of who she truly is.

Delphi's true purpose is revealed: she is the secret daughter of Voldemort and Bellatrix Lestrange, and she has used the boys all along to reach the past and restore her father's power. She seizes the Time-Turner, strands and threatens Albus and Scorpius, and travels to Godric's Hollow on the night in 1981 when Voldemort attacked the infant Harry, meaning to stop the curse that destroyed him. The boys contrive a way to summon Harry, Ginny, Ron, Hermione, and Draco to that night. Together they confront and overpower Delphi, and Harry endures the agony of watching his own parents die rather than let history be broken, so that Voldemort's downfall unfolds as it truly did. Delphi is captured and imprisoned. In the calm afterward, Harry and Albus finally reach each other, their long estrangement healing into understanding, and Harry and Draco's old enmity gives way to a wary respect. Having learned that some griefs cannot and should not be undone, the two families face the future together.

characters.description: The young wizard at the centre of the story, now seventeen and marked from infancy by the dark wizard Voldemort, who killed his parents and has hunted him ever since. Rather than return to Hogwarts, Harry has taken up the task his late mentor Dumbledore left him: to find and destroy the hidden objects in which Voldemort has concealed pieces of his soul, making himself hard to kill. Brave, stubborn, and burdened by grief and responsibility, he begins the book a wanted fugitive as Voldemort's forces close in.
characters.name: Harry Potter

characters.description: Harry's closest friend, from a large and loving wizarding family that has sheltered and stood by him for years. Loyal and brave but prone to self-doubt and jealousy, he chooses to abandon his own schooling and safety to help Harry hunt down Voldemort's hidden soul-fragments. He faces the danger alongside Harry and Hermione, his family now a target because of their known loyalties.
characters.name: Ron Weasley

characters.description: Harry's brilliant, resourceful friend, born to non-magical parents, who has protected her family by wiping their memories of her and sending them away. The most learned and prepared of the three, she has packed everything they might need into an enchanted bag and repeatedly keeps the group alive with careful planning and quick spellwork. She joins Harry and Ron on the hunt for Voldemort's soul-fragments, giving up her final year of school.
characters.name: Hermione Granger

characters.description: The dark wizard who has now effectively seized power over the wizarding world, controlling the government and Hogwarts through terror and his followers. Obsessed with killing Harry and with his own immortality, he opens the book gathering his Death Eaters to plan Harry's death, and grows fixated on obtaining a legendary unbeatable wand. Cruel and fearless of death, he does not know that his hold on life depends on hidden objects Harry is seeking to destroy.
characters.name: Lord Voldemort

characters.description: The Potions master turned headmaster, who killed Dumbledore at the end of the previous year and now appears to be one of Voldemort's most trusted servants, installed in command of Hogwarts. Cold and unreadable, he sits among the Death Eaters as the book opens, and to Harry and nearly everyone else he is a murderer and a traitor. His true loyalties are a mystery that hangs over the story.
characters.name: Severus Snape

characters.description: The late headmaster of Hogwarts, killed the year before, who set Harry the task of destroying Voldemort's hidden soul-fragments but died leaving much unexplained. In this book he appears only through memory, letters, and a newly published, unflattering biography that dredges up secrets from his youth. Harry, grieving and increasingly uncertain, is forced to question how well he ever really knew the man whose plans he is trying to carry out.
characters.name: Albus Dumbledore

characters.description: The huge, warm-hearted gamekeeper of Hogwarts and one of Harry's oldest friends, unfailingly devoted to him and to Dumbledore's memory. Loyal to the point of recklessness, he takes part in the dangerous operation to move Harry to safety as the forces of Voldemort hunt him, insisting on protecting the boy he first brought into the wizarding world.
characters.name: Rubeus Hagrid

characters.description: A fanatically devoted follower of Voldemort, cruel and unstable, who revels in her master's power and in causing pain. Present when the Death Eaters gather at the opening, she is among the most dangerous of Voldemort's servants and takes fierce pride in her closeness to him. She holds old grudges against those who have opposed her side.
characters.name: Bellatrix Lestrange

characters.description: Ron's younger sister, a spirited and capable witch and the youngest of the Weasley children, who has grown close to Harry. Still of school age and so unable to join the hunt, she remains behind with her family, whose open loyalty to Harry and to the resistance puts them all in danger. Brave and strong-willed, she chafes at being kept out of the fight.
characters.name: Ginny Weasley

characters.description: An aged, muttering house-elf bound in servitude to the old wizarding house Harry has inherited, long embittered and disloyal. When the three fugitives take refuge in that house, Kreacher's grudging cooperation and the story he tells about a past master turn out to hold a vital clue to one of the objects Harry is hunting.
characters.name: Kreacher

characters.description: A free house-elf who has adored Harry ever since Harry secured his freedom years earlier, and who has quietly watched over him. Fearless in Harry's defence and unbound by any master, he answers a desperate call for help when the friends are captured and held prisoner, arriving to attempt a rescue against impossible odds.
characters.name: Dobby

characters.description: Harry's brave but once-timid classmate, who has stayed at Hogwarts through the year of Death Eater rule and grown into a leader of the student resistance against it. Battered and defiant, he keeps the spirit of opposition alive within the school and rallies to Harry the moment he returns, ready to fight.
characters.name: Neville Longbottom

recaps.ending: In the Battle of Hogwarts, the last of Voldemort's Horcruxes fall: Ron and Hermione destroy Hufflepuff's cup, the diadem is consumed by cursed fire, and Voldemort's snake Nagini is beheaded by Neville with the sword of Gryffindor. Voldemort kills Snape, believing it will make him master of an unbeatable wand, but Snape's final memories show he was Dumbledore's loyal agent, driven by lifelong love for Harry's mother, and that Harry is himself an unintended Horcrux who must die. Harry walks into the forest and lets Voldemort strike him down without defending himself. Because Voldemort had earlier used Harry's blood to rebuild his body, Harry does not truly die; he meets Dumbledore in a vision and chooses to return. Voldemort's killing curse had destroyed only the fragment of soul within Harry. In the final confrontation Harry reveals that he, not Snape, is the true master of the unbeatable Elder Wand, so it will not work against him; Voldemort's own curse rebounds and kills him for good. Many have died in the fighting, including Fred Weasley, Lupin, and Tonks, but Voldemort is destroyed. An epilogue set nineteen years later shows Harry married to Ginny, and Ron married to Hermione, seeing their own children off to Hogwarts in a world finally at peace.
recaps.in_short: Harry, Ron, and Hermione abandon school to hunt down the Horcruxes, the hidden objects holding pieces of Voldemort's soul that keep him alive. On the run as Voldemort seizes control of the government and Hogwarts, they destroy a locket, learn of three legendary objects called the Deathly Hallows, and are captured and taken to Malfoy Manor, where the house-elf Dobby dies saving them. Breaking into a bank vault, they claim another Horcrux and later infiltrate Hogwarts to find one more. A great battle erupts at the school. Snape is killed by Voldemort, but his dying memories reveal that he loved Harry's mother, worked secretly for Dumbledore all along, and that Harry himself is an accidental Horcrux who must die for Voldemort to be mortal. Harry lets Voldemort strike him down, survives, and returns. Neville destroys the last Horcrux, and in a final duel Voldemort's own killing curse rebounds and kills him. Nineteen years later, Harry and his friends are grown, married, and sending their own children off to Hogwarts.

recaps.text: Over his six years at Hogwarts, Harry Potter has grown from a bullied orphan into the wizarding world's symbol of resistance against the dark wizard Voldemort, who killed his parents when Harry was a baby. A prophecy has marked the two of them as bound to face each other, with neither able to truly live while the other survives. After years in hiding, Voldemort has returned to a full body and openly regained his power, and the Ministry of Magic and much of society have fallen under his influence. At the close of the previous year, Harry learned Voldemort's central secret: he has split his soul into pieces and hidden them in concealed objects called Horcruxes, which anchor him to life and must all be destroyed before he can be killed. Dumbledore, the headmaster who had become Harry's guide and had begun hunting these objects with him, was killed by Professor Snape, apparently a traitor. As this book opens Harry is seventeen, grieving, and resolved to leave school with his closest friends Ron and Hermione to finish Dumbledore's task and find the remaining Horcruxes, while Voldemort's followers hunt him.

Voldemort gathers his Death Eaters and confirms that the government and Hogwarts are now under his control, and they plan to capture Harry the moment he leaves the protection of his relatives' home. Harry prepares to go, and the Order of the Phoenix mounts an operation to move him to safety: several friends drink a potion to take Harry's exact appearance, so that seven identical Harrys set out in different directions to confuse the enemy. Voldemort and his followers attack them in the air. In the chaos Harry's pet owl Hedwig is killed, the veteran Order member Mad-Eye Moody dies, and George Weasley is badly wounded, but Harry escapes and the survivors regroup at the Weasley family home. The war has plainly begun, and the safety Harry once relied on is gone.

An official from the Ministry delivers items Dumbledore left to Harry, Ron, and Hermione in his will, including a strange golden ball, an old book of children's tales, and a device that captures light; the reasons behind the gifts are unclear, and a promised sword is withheld. At the wedding of Ron's brother Bill, the celebration is shattered when word arrives that the Ministry has fallen to Voldemort and the government is now his. Death Eaters descend on the gathering, and Harry, Ron, and Hermione are forced to flee together, abandoning their families and the wedding, and going into hiding with no clear plan beyond survival and the search for the Horcruxes.

The three take refuge in the old London house Harry has inherited, where its resentful house-elf, Kreacher, tells them the story of a locket Horcrux and the master who tried to destroy it, revealing that it was stolen years ago by a petty thief. They track the thief down and learn the locket has since passed to a cruel Ministry official. To recover it, the three disguise themselves and infiltrate the Ministry of Magic, now openly persecuting wizards born to non-magical families. They rescue frightened prisoners and seize the locket, but their cover is broken and they must flee for good, unable to return to the house, now on the run with no safe base and one Horcrux they cannot yet destroy.

Living rough in the wilderness, the three grow cold, hungry, and frayed, and the evil locket, which they take turns wearing, poisons their moods. Ron, worn down and jealous, quarrels with Harry and abandons the group, leaving Harry and Hermione alone. The two visit Harry's birthplace, Godric's Hollow, hoping for answers, but it is a trap: Voldemort's snake attacks them in disguise, and they barely escape, with Harry's wand broken in the flight. Harry then follows a mysterious silver doe, a protective spirit sent by an unknown helper, to a frozen pool where the lost sword of Gryffindor lies. Ron reappears at that moment, saves Harry from the locket's magic as he tries to retrieve the sword, and uses the blade to destroy the locket Horcrux. Reunited and one step closer, the friends press on.

The friends learn of the Deathly Hallows, three legendary objects, an unbeatable wand, a stone that recalls the dead, and a cloak of true invisibility, that together are said to master death, and Harry becomes gripped by the idea of uniting them, torn between chasing the Hallows and hunting the Horcruxes. Captured by scavengers and taken to the Malfoy family's manor, they are held prisoner while Hermione is tortured by the fanatic Bellatrix Lestrange for information about a break-in. The loyal house-elf Dobby appears and rescues them, spiriting them away, but is killed in the escape. Sheltering afterward, they question a captive wandmaker and a goblin and resolve to break into a heavily guarded bank vault where they believe another Horcrux is hidden, while Voldemort, they realize, is himself now searching for the unbeatable wand.

With the goblin's help the three break into the deep vault of the Lestrange family and seize a golden cup that is another of Voldemort's Horcruxes, then escape by freeing and riding out on a captive dragon. Harry senses that a final Horcrux is hidden at Hogwarts itself, and the three make their way to the village beside the school, where Dumbledore's estranged brother Aberforth shelters them and opens a secret passage into the castle. Inside, they find that the students have kept a resistance alive through the year of Death Eater rule, and old friends rally to Harry. As they begin searching for the hidden object, the alarm is raised, Voldemort learns Harry is there, and the school braces for open battle.

The teachers and students drive out the Death Eater in charge and fortify the castle, and the Battle of Hogwarts begins as Voldemort's army attacks. Amid the fighting the friends find the hidden Horcrux, an old diadem, in a vast storeroom, where it is destroyed by cursed fire that also kills one of their attackers. Voldemort, convinced that killing the supposed owner of the unbeatable wand will make it truly his, has his snake kill Snape. As Snape dies he gives Harry a flood of memories, which reveal the truth: Snape had loved Harry's mother since childhood, had turned against Voldemort after her death, and had served Dumbledore faithfully all along, even carrying out Dumbledore's own dying wish by killing him. The memories also reveal the hardest truth of all, that a fragment of Voldemort's soul lives inside Harry himself, so that Harry must let Voldemort kill him before Voldemort can finally die.

Accepting what he must do, Harry walks unarmed into the forest and lets Voldemort strike him down without defending himself. But because Voldemort had earlier rebuilt his body using Harry's blood, Harry is not truly killed; the curse destroys only the piece of Voldemort's soul inside him. In a vision Harry meets Dumbledore, learns the full story, and chooses to return to life. Feigning death, he is carried back to the castle, where the fighting resumes. Neville Longbottom beheads Voldemort's snake, the last Horcrux, with the sword of Gryffindor, making Voldemort mortal at last. In the final duel Harry reveals that he, not Snape, is the true master of Voldemort's unbeatable wand, because of how its ownership had passed, so the wand will not turn against him. Voldemort's own killing curse rebounds and destroys him for good. The war is won, though at great cost in lives, including Ron's brother Fred and the friends Lupin and Tonks. The wizarding world is freed, and Harry, wanting no more power, gives up the unbeatable wand.

characters.description: Now fourteen and in his fourth year, Harry wakes from a dream of Voldemort plotting a murder, his scar aching. Famous and increasingly aware of the darkness gathering around him, he is thrust unwillingly into a deadly school tournament meant only for older students, and must cope with sudden hostile attention he never asked for.
characters.name: Harry Potter

characters.description: Harry's best friend, who brings him to the Quidditch World Cup with his family. This year his loyalty is tested when he becomes convinced Harry entered the dangerous tournament for glory and lied about it, and the two fall out for weeks before the truth pulls them back together.
characters.name: Ron Weasley

characters.description: Harry and Ron's clever, principled friend, who keeps her head when the two boys quarrel and stands by Harry throughout the tournament. She throws herself into a campaign for the rights of house-elves and draws the notice, and later the malice, of a gossip journalist covering the contest.
characters.name: Hermione Granger

characters.description: The dark wizard, still weak and barely more than a shadow of himself, glimpsed plotting in a ruined house with a servant. He is patiently working toward a scheme to restore his body and full power, and Harry's scar burns with the sense of his growing strength.
characters.name: Lord Voldemort

characters.description: The cowardly wizard who betrayed Harry's parents to Voldemort and framed Sirius Black, now serving as the weakened Voldemort's sole helper. Fearful and grovelling, he tends his master's frail form and carries out his cruelties, having nowhere left to go but back to the dark wizard's side.
characters.name: Peter Pettigrew

characters.description: A well-liked, honest older Hufflepuff student and an accomplished Quidditch player, whom Harry first meets travelling to the Quidditch World Cup. Modest and fair-minded, he is admired across the school and becomes one of its champions in the coming tournament.
characters.name: Cedric Diggory

characters.description: A stiff, correct senior Ministry official who oversees international magical cooperation and helps organize the tournament. Once tipped as a future Minister for Magic, he is a stickler for rules whose rigid manner hides some private strain.
characters.name: Barty Crouch

characters.description: The new Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher, a legendary retired dark-wizard catcher famous for filling half of Azkaban. Battle-scarred, with a wooden leg and a magical, ceaselessly swivelling blue eye, he is gruff, paranoid, and endlessly watchful, and he teaches his students by confronting them directly with the darkest curses.
characters.name: Alastor Moody

characters.description: A famous international Quidditch star, chosen as champion for the visiting Durmstrang school. Surly and awkward off the pitch and much admired on it, he takes a quiet, genuine interest in Hermione.
characters.name: Viktor Krum

characters.description: The champion chosen for the visiting Beauxbatons Academy, a striking young woman, part magical veela, who is poised and proud and initially dismissive of Harry as too young to belong in the contest.
characters.name: Fleur Delacour

characters.description: A gossip columnist for the wizarding newspaper, known for sensational, largely invented stories. She corners Harry for interviews and prints damaging, fabricated accounts of him and those close to him, feeding on the tournament's drama.
characters.name: Rita Skeeter

characters.description: The Hogwarts headmaster, presiding over the tournament while quietly alert to signs that Voldemort's followers are stirring. He believes Harry did not enter the contest himself and watches over him, increasingly certain that darker events are moving beneath the surface of the year's festivities.
characters.name: Albus Dumbledore

recaps.ending: The Triwizard Tournament ends in tragedy. Harry and Cedric Diggory agree to take the cup together as a shared Hogwarts victory, but it is a Portkey that whisks them to a distant graveyard. There, on Voldemort's order, the servant Wormtail kills Cedric and uses Harry's blood, along with Wormtail's own flesh and the bone of Voldemort's dead father, in a ritual that restores Voldemort to a body and full power. Voldemort summons his Death Eaters and duels Harry, but when their wands lock, an effect of their twin cores forces echoes of Voldemort's recent victims, including Harry's parents and Cedric, to emerge and shield Harry, letting him escape with Cedric's body. Back at Hogwarts, the Defence teacher Mad-Eye Moody is exposed as an impostor, the Death Eater Barty Crouch Jr in disguise, who entered Harry in the tournament and steered him to the trap. Dumbledore believes Harry and begins rallying allies for the coming war, but the Minister for Magic, Fudge, refuses to accept that Voldemort has returned, and the wizarding world splits between those who believe and those who deny it. The school year ends in grief, with Voldemort restored and free.
recaps.in_short: In his fourth year, Harry is mysteriously entered into the Triwizard Tournament, a dangerous contest between three magical schools normally limited to older students, becoming a fourth champion alongside Cedric Diggory, Viktor Krum, and Fleur Delacour. Much of the school believes he cheated, and he faces three deadly tasks: getting past a dragon, rescuing hostages from a lake, and navigating an enchanted maze. Throughout, signs point to Voldemort's return, and Harry's scar troubles him. Harry and Cedric reach the tournament cup together and grab it at the same moment, only to find it is a trap that transports them to a graveyard. There Cedric is murdered and Voldemort, using Harry's blood in a dark ritual, regains his body and full power. Harry escapes and returns with Cedric's body. The disguised Death Eater who engineered everything is exposed, but the Minister for Magic refuses to believe Voldemort is back, leaving the wizarding world divided as open war threatens.

recaps.text: Harry Potter was orphaned as a baby when the dark wizard Lord Voldemort killed his parents and was defeated attempting to kill him. Raised by his unkind relatives, he learned at eleven that he is a wizard, went to Hogwarts, was sorted into Gryffindor, and befriended loyal Ron Weasley and brilliant Hermione Granger. Over three years he stopped Voldemort from stealing the immortality-granting Philosopher's Stone; killed a monster and destroyed a diary holding the teenage Voldemort's memory beneath the school; and learned that his godfather, Sirius Black, wrongly imprisoned for betraying his parents, was innocent, the real traitor being Peter Pettigrew, who escaped to rejoin his master. Voldemort has survived every year as a weakened, disembodied remnant. Dumbledore, the headmaster, has long warned that the dark wizard means to return to full power, and the signs that he is close have been mounting.

The book opens with a chilling scene: in the ruin of the Riddle family house, the weak, shrunken Voldemort and his servant Wormtail plot a murder and kill an elderly Muggle caretaker who overhears them. Harry wakes from a dream of this with his scar burning, worried by what it might mean, and writes to his godfather Sirius Black, now in hiding. Soon the Weasleys collect Harry from the Dursleys, using magical Floo travel that goes comically wrong, and take him to the Quidditch World Cup. Harry meets Cedric Diggory, an admired older student, on the way. The friends enjoy the spectacle of the international match, in which the young star Viktor Krum plays for Bulgaria, unaware that the festivities are about to turn frightening.

In the night after the World Cup final, masked Death Eaters, Voldemort's followers, rampage through the campground, terrorizing Muggles and sending the crowd fleeing in panic. In the chaos someone conjures the Dark Mark, Voldemort's skull-and-serpent sign, into the sky for the first time in thirteen years, a sight that horrifies the wizarding world and hints that his supporters are growing bold again. Harry realizes his wand has gone missing and was used to cast the Mark, and a tense Ministry inquiry follows. The events leave the adults deeply uneasy and Harry more certain that something dark is stirring. The friends return to the Weasleys' home and prepare to go back to Hogwarts, with rumours swirling that an unusual and exciting event is planned at the school for the coming year.

At school the students learn that Hogwarts will host the Triwizard Tournament, a dangerous historic contest between three magical schools, with one champion each chosen by an impartial magical judge, the Goblet of Fire, and entry restricted to students of seventeen and over. A gruff, battle-scarred new Defence teacher, Mad-Eye Moody, arrives and shocks the class by demonstrating the three Unforgivable Curses. The rival schools, Beauxbatons and Durmstrang, arrive with their students, including Fleur Delacour and Viktor Krum. The Goblet selects three champions, Cedric, Fleur, and Krum, and then, impossibly, spits out a fourth name: Harry Potter, who is underage and swears he did not enter. Bound by magic to compete, and disbelieved by nearly everyone including Ron, who stops speaking to him, Harry faces the first task and gets past a fierce dragon by summoning his broom and outflying it, after which Ron, realizing the danger was real, makes up with him.

Between tasks the champions face the awkward social pressures of the Yule Ball, and Harry and Ron fumble their way through dates while Hermione attends with Viktor Krum, stirring Ron's jealousy. The gossip writer Rita Skeeter prints spiteful, invented stories about Harry and his friends. Cedric quietly repays Harry's earlier warning about the dragon by helping him understand the clue to the second task. In that task the champions must dive into the lake to rescue people dear to them held by the merpeople; Harry, taking the rules too literally, stays to help free the others and finishes last but is praised for his nerve. Meanwhile Barty Crouch, the rigid Ministry official who organized the tournament, stops appearing and behaves strangely, and Harry's scar continues to trouble him as his letters with Sirius grow more urgent.

Exploring the grounds at night, Harry and Krum find Barty Crouch wandering and raving, apparently ill and speaking as though to Voldemort, before he vanishes; he is never found alive. Investigating in Dumbledore's office, Harry falls into the headmaster's Pensieve, a device for viewing memories, and witnesses old trials from the last war: the cruel Death Eater Bellatrix Lestrange and, most strikingly, Crouch's own son being sentenced to Azkaban for torturing an Auror family. The revelations deepen Harry's dread. Sirius warns him that the tournament may be a cover for something aimed at him, and that enemies are close. Harry's scar hurts more often. With the mystery of Crouch's fate unsolved and a sense of a trap tightening, the champions are shown the vast, hedged maze grown for the final task, at the heart of which waits the Triwizard Cup.

In the final task Harry and Cedric help each other through the dangers of the maze and reach the cup together, agreeing to claim it as one for Hogwarts, but it is a Portkey that transports them both to a graveyard far away. There Wormtail murders Cedric on Voldemort's command and uses Harry's blood in a dark ritual, along with a bone of Voldemort's father and Wormtail's own hand, to restore Voldemort to a body and full power. Voldemort summons his Death Eaters, boasts of his return, and duels Harry, but when their twin-cored wands connect, ghostly echoes of his recent victims, including Cedric and Harry's parents, spill out and shield Harry, allowing him to seize Cedric's body and escape back to Hogwarts by Portkey. There the impostor is unmasked: the Defence teacher Moody was really the escaped Death Eater Barty Crouch Jr, disguised all year, who entered Harry in the tournament to deliver him to his master. Dumbledore believes Harry and begins gathering allies, but the Minister for Magic, Fudge, refuses to accept that Voldemort has returned. The year ends in mourning, the wizarding world divided, and Voldemort loose and whole once more.

characters.description: Sixteen and, since Voldemort's return became public, a celebrated figure rather than a doubted one. Grieving his godfather Sirius and trusted by Dumbledore with private lessons, Harry spends the year both learning Voldemort's history and obsessively convinced that Draco Malfoy has become a servant of the enemy, a suspicion nobody else takes seriously.
characters.name: Harry Potter

characters.description: Harry's best friend, now a Gryffindor Quidditch keeper and tangled up in the awkward romances of their sixth year. His clumsy relationship with a classmate and his prickliness with Hermione strain the friends' good humour, but he stays firmly at Harry's side as the danger grows.
characters.name: Ron Weasley

characters.description: Harry and Ron's brilliant friend, whose feelings for Ron and jealousy over his romance run through the year alongside her usual sharp research. She is sceptical of Harry's fixation on Draco and uneasy about the mysterious old textbook that is making Harry so good at potions.
characters.name: Hermione Granger

characters.description: The Hogwarts headmaster, who collects Harry personally this summer and begins meeting him privately to explore Voldemort's past through gathered memories. His right hand is mysteriously blackened and withered, and he is more openly mortal and more determined than ever, working toward a secret plan to bring about Voldemort's downfall.
characters.name: Albus Dumbledore

characters.description: The Potions master, who at last gains the Defence Against the Dark Arts post he has long wanted. In the book's opening he makes an Unbreakable Vow to Narcissa Malfoy, swearing to protect and assist her son Draco and, if Draco fails, to finish a task himself, though the nature of that task is kept hidden.
characters.name: Severus Snape

characters.description: Harry's rival, withdrawn and frightened this year beneath his usual sneer. With his father imprisoned after the Ministry battle, Harry is convinced Voldemort has set him some grim task and, watching him slip away to the castle's forgotten corners, that Draco is now a Death Eater working from within the school.
characters.name: Draco Malfoy

characters.description: Ron's spirited younger sister, now a popular and confident girl and a talented Quidditch player. Over the year Harry finds his feelings for her deepening into something he has to keep pushing down, complicated by her being his best friend's sister.
characters.name: Ginny Weasley

characters.description: A genial, well-connected retired Hogwarts teacher whom Dumbledore coaxes back to teach Potions. He loves to collect promising and famous students and cultivate their favour, and he carries a guilty secret from his past that Dumbledore badly needs Harry to draw out of him.
characters.name: Horace Slughorn

characters.description: Draco's mother, desperate to protect her son now that her husband is imprisoned and Voldemort has set Draco a dangerous task. Defying the Dark Lord's wishes, she secretly seeks out Snape and begs his help, binding him to a magical oath to shield her boy.
characters.name: Narcissa Malfoy

characters.description: Narcissa's sister and a fanatically loyal servant of Voldemort. Distrustful and cruel, she accompanies Narcissa to Snape's house and tries to catch him out in disloyalty, doubting that he truly serves the Dark Lord.
characters.name: Bellatrix Lestrange

characters.description: The dark lord, now openly returned and terrorizing both wizards and Muggles. This year Dumbledore shares gathered memories that trace his history, from his birth as the orphan Tom Riddle, through a cold and manipulative boyhood, to his transformation into Voldemort, all in search of the secret to how he has cheated death.
characters.name: Lord Voldemort

characters.description: The unknown former owner of a second-hand Potions textbook Harry is given, who filled its margins with improved instructions and invented spells and signed it 'the Half-Blood Prince.' The notes make Harry brilliant at potions and fascinate him, but he cannot discover who the Prince was, and some of the scrawled spells prove darker than they first seem.
characters.name: the Half-Blood Prince

recaps.ending: Half-Blood Prince ends with Dumbledore's death and Harry's turn toward the final fight. Returning from a mission to destroy one of Voldemort's Horcruxes, the soul-fragments that keep him from dying, Dumbledore and an exhausted Harry find the Dark Mark over Hogwarts: Draco Malfoy has smuggled Death Eaters into the castle through a repaired vanishing cabinet. On the astronomy tower Draco disarms Dumbledore but cannot make himself commit murder, and Snape arrives and kills Dumbledore, then escapes, revealing as he flees that he is the Half-Blood Prince whose old textbook Harry had relied on all year. The locket Dumbledore and Harry retrieved from the cave, at terrible cost, turns out to be a fake, left in place of the real Horcrux by an unknown thief who signs only 'R.A.B.' Dumbledore is buried at Hogwarts, and the school may not reopen. Harry ends his budding romance with Ginny to keep her out of danger, and, with Ron and Hermione pledging to come with him, decides not to return for a final year but to find and destroy Voldemort's remaining Horcruxes so that the Dark Lord can at last be killed. Voldemort is ascendant, Snape has fled to his side, and the war is entering its darkest phase.
recaps.in_short: With war now open, Harry's sixth year mixes ordinary school life with Dumbledore's quiet campaign against Voldemort. Dumbledore gives Harry private lessons, using collected memories to trace Voldemort's history from his orphan boyhood as Tom Riddle. Harry excels at Potions thanks to an old textbook annotated by a mysterious 'Half-Blood Prince,' and grows sure that Draco Malfoy has become a Death Eater plotting something inside the castle. Using a lucky potion, Harry retrieves a hidden memory revealing Voldemort's secret to immortality: Horcruxes, objects into which he split his soul, several of which must be destroyed to make him mortal. Dumbledore and Harry go to a hidden cave to destroy one, returning to find Death Eaters have breached Hogwarts through Draco's scheme. On the tower, Draco cannot bring himself to kill Dumbledore, and Snape does it instead, then flees, revealing that he was the Half-Blood Prince. The retrieved Horcrux proves a fake. Dumbledore is dead, and Harry resolves to leave school and hunt the remaining Horcruxes.

recaps.text: Harry Potter, orphaned when Lord Voldemort killed his parents and was defeated trying to kill him, learned at eleven that he is a wizard, went to Hogwarts, joined Gryffindor, and befriended Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger. Over five years he thwarted Voldemort's schemes again and again: stopping the theft of the Philosopher's Stone, destroying a diary holding the young Voldemort's memory, and clearing his godfather Sirius Black. Forced into a deadly tournament, he saw Voldemort restored to a body using his blood, and the following year, persecuted by a Ministry in denial, he formed a secret student defence group. That year ended at the Ministry of Magic, where Sirius was killed and Voldemort was at last seen publicly, forcing the world to admit he had returned. Harry learned a prophecy binding him to Voldemort: neither can live while the other survives. The war is now open, and Dumbledore, the headmaster, has begun preparing Harry for the confrontation that only one of them can survive.

The wizarding world is now openly at war, with Voldemort's followers spreading fear and death and the Ministry struggling to cope. In a shadowy scene, Snape makes an Unbreakable Vow to Draco Malfoy's mother, Narcissa, swearing to protect Draco and to complete a mysterious task himself if the boy fails. Dumbledore collects Harry from the Dursleys in person and takes him to recruit an old colleague, Horace Slughorn, back to Hogwarts as Potions teacher. Dumbledore reveals that he will give Harry private lessons this year, and that his own hand has been badly and mysteriously injured. On a subdued shopping trip to Diagon Alley, Harry secretly follows Draco to a shop selling dark objects and comes away convinced that Draco is up to something sinister, perhaps that he has become a Death Eater.

Term begins with Harry made Quidditch captain and unexpectedly excelling in Potions, thanks to a battered second-hand textbook crammed with the improved instructions and invented spells of a previous owner who signed himself the Half-Blood Prince. Dumbledore's private lessons start, and together he and Harry begin exploring memories of Voldemort's past: his birth to a poor, abandoned mother, and his cold, frightening childhood in an orphanage as the boy Tom Riddle, who was already cruel and drawn to power before Dumbledore ever brought him to Hogwarts. Dumbledore is clearly building toward some vital secret. He shows Harry a tampered memory belonging to Slughorn, from which a crucial piece has been removed, and asks Harry to use his growing closeness with the new teacher to recover the true version.

The sixth-years are caught up in romances and jealousies: Ron takes up with a clingy classmate, driving a wedge between him and Hermione, while Harry finds himself increasingly drawn to Ron's sister, Ginny. Beneath the ordinary school year, danger presses in. A student is gravely cursed by a necklace clearly meant for someone else, and Harry is certain Draco is behind it and is trying to reach Dumbledore, though the adults dismiss his suspicions. Dumbledore continues showing Harry memories of the young Voldemort, including one in which the teenage Riddle questioned Slughorn about a piece of very dark magic, the missing part of the memory Dumbledore still needs. Slughorn, ashamed, refuses to give up the true recollection, and Harry cannot yet coax it from him.

Danger keeps striking close: Ron is nearly killed by poisoned drink apparently intended for Dumbledore, further proof to Harry that someone inside the school is trying to murder the headmaster. During a confrontation in a bathroom Harry uses an unknown spell from the Prince's book against Draco and badly wounds him, horrified at what the scrawled curse does. Finally, dosing himself with a potion of pure luck, Harry succeeds where nothing else worked and draws the true memory out of Slughorn. It reveals Voldemort's terrible secret: he asked Slughorn about Horcruxes, objects into which a wizard can split his soul to escape death, and boasted of intending to make several. Dumbledore concludes that Voldemort made multiple Horcruxes, and that each must be found and destroyed before Voldemort himself can be killed.

Dumbledore takes Harry to a hidden seaside cave to retrieve one of the Horcruxes, a locket, forcing himself to drink a torturous potion to reach it and returning gravely weakened. They come back to find the Dark Mark over Hogwarts: Draco has smuggled Death Eaters into the castle through a repaired magical cabinet. On the astronomy tower Draco disarms Dumbledore and admits he was ordered to kill him, but cannot bring himself to do it. Snape arrives and kills Dumbledore, then flees the castle, revealing to Harry as he goes that he himself is the Half-Blood Prince. Worse, the locket they nearly died for is a fake, containing a note from a thief signed only 'R.A.B.,' meaning the real Horcrux is still out there. Dumbledore is buried on the grounds, the school's future in doubt. Harry breaks off his new relationship with Ginny to keep her safe and resolves not to return for a final year, but to seek out and destroy Voldemort's remaining Horcruxes; Ron and Hermione vow to go with him.

characters.description: Fifteen and increasingly angry, Harry begins the year isolated and frustrated: haunted by Cedric's death, cut off from news, and disbelieved when he insists that Voldemort has returned. Branded a liar by the wizarding press and the Ministry, he struggles with his temper and a growing, disturbing link to Voldemort's mind, while shouldering more than any boy his age should have to.
characters.name: Harry Potter

characters.description: Harry's steadfast friend, staying with his family at the headquarters of a secret anti-Voldemort society. Made a Gryffindor prefect this year alongside Hermione, he grows into a little more responsibility while remaining loyal to Harry through the isolation and suspicion Harry faces.
characters.name: Ron Weasley

characters.description: Harry and Ron's clever, level-headed friend, who becomes a Gryffindor prefect and the strategist behind the students' resistance to the Ministry's grip on the school. She persuades Harry to secretly teach his classmates real defensive magic and manages his temper with patience and sense.
characters.name: Hermione Granger

characters.description: Harry's godfather, cleared in no one's eyes but Harry's and still a wanted fugitive, who shelters the secret society in his gloomy ancestral home. Reckless and restless at being confined and useless, he is the closest thing to a parent Harry has, and chafes bitterly at being unable to protect him openly.
characters.name: Sirius Black

characters.description: A young, cheerful Auror and member of the secret society guarding Harry, able to change her appearance at will. Clumsy but warm, she lightens the grim mood of the society's headquarters and helps escort Harry safely to it.
characters.name: Nymphadora Tonks

characters.description: A Ministry official, sweet-voiced and fond of pink and kittens but coldly authoritarian, who appears first at Harry's disciplinary hearing and is then installed as the Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher. She refuses to teach any practical magic, punishes dissent with cruel detentions, and steadily seizes control of the school on the Ministry's behalf.
characters.name: Dolores Umbridge

characters.description: A dreamy, serenely odd student in Ginny's year, whom Harry meets on the train. She believes in many things others mock, wears strange homemade jewellery, and speaks her mind without embarrassment, but she is loyal, unafraid, and more perceptive than she first appears.
characters.name: Luna Lovegood

characters.description: Ron's younger sister, no longer the shy girl of earlier years but confident, quick-tongued, and unafraid to stand up to her brothers or to Harry. She becomes a committed member of the students' secret defence group and a capable young witch in her own right.
characters.name: Ginny Weasley

characters.description: Harry's clumsy, good-hearted classmate, who joins the secret defence group and works harder at it than anyone. He lives with his grandmother; his parents were tortured into madness by Voldemort's followers, a loss that gives his determination a quiet, private weight.
characters.name: Neville Longbottom

characters.description: The Hogwarts headmaster, now openly opposed by a Ministry that fears he is raising an army, and stripped of his official positions for insisting Voldemort has returned. This year he avoids Harry's eyes and keeps him at a strange distance, for reasons Harry cannot understand and finds deeply hurtful.
characters.name: Albus Dumbledore

characters.description: The Potions master, tasked by Dumbledore with teaching Harry to close his mind against Voldemort's intrusions. The lessons go badly, poisoned by their mutual loathing.
characters.name: Severus Snape

characters.description: A fanatically devoted follower of Voldemort and one of his most dangerous, who escapes Azkaban in a mass breakout. Cruel, unhinged, and proud of her loyalty, she is Sirius Black's cousin and was among those who tortured Neville Longbottom's parents into madness.
characters.name: Bellatrix Lestrange

recaps.ending: Harry's fifth year ends in loss and grim clarity. Tricked by a false vision, Harry leads his friends to the Ministry of Magic to rescue his godfather Sirius, only to find it was a lure: Voldemort wanted Harry to retrieve a prophecy that only he could take from the Hall of Prophecy. Death Eaters attack, the young wizards fight desperately, and members of the Order of the Phoenix arrive to help; in the battle Sirius is struck by his cousin Bellatrix Lestrange and falls through a mysterious veil to his death. Voldemort himself appears and duels Dumbledore, and the Minister for Magic, Fudge, sees him with his own eyes, so the wizarding world can no longer deny that Voldemort has returned. Voldemort briefly possesses Harry and then flees. Afterward Dumbledore finally explains the prophecy and why he kept his distance all year: Harry and Voldemort are bound so that neither can live while the other survives, and one must ultimately kill the other, which is why Voldemort marked Harry as a baby. Fudge is discredited, the Ministry mobilizes for open war, and Harry, grieving Sirius and burdened with his destiny, returns to the Dursleys knowing what lies ahead.
recaps.in_short: With Voldemort returned but the Ministry of Magic denying it and branding Harry a liar, Harry's fifth year is one of official persecution. He is taken to the headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix, the secret society fighting Voldemort. At school the Ministry installs Dolores Umbridge, who bans practical Defence lessons and seizes ever more power, so Harry secretly teaches his classmates to fight, forming Dumbledore's Army. Harry suffers visions through a growing mental link to Voldemort and is made to take Occlumency lessons with Snape to shut it. When he sees his godfather Sirius being tortured, he leads friends to the Ministry to save him, but it is a trap: Voldemort lured him to retrieve a prophecy about the two of them. In the battle Sirius is killed by Bellatrix Lestrange. Voldemort's public appearance finally forces the Ministry to admit he is back. Dumbledore reveals the prophecy: Harry and Voldemort are fated to face each other, and only one can survive.

recaps.text: Harry Potter, orphaned as a baby when Lord Voldemort killed his parents and was defeated trying to kill him, learned at eleven that he is a wizard and went to Hogwarts, where he was sorted into Gryffindor and befriended Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger. Over four years he foiled Voldemort's attempt to steal the Philosopher's Stone; destroyed a diary holding the young Voldemort's memory; cleared his wrongly imprisoned godfather, Sirius Black, of betraying his parents; and, forced into a deadly school tournament, watched the Death Eater Wormtail murder the student Cedric Diggory and use Harry's blood to restore Voldemort to a body and full power. Harry escaped, but the Minister for Magic, Fudge, refused to believe Voldemort had returned and began treating Harry and the headmaster, Dumbledore, as troublemakers. Voldemort is now back, whole and gathering strength, while the Ministry denies it and the wizarding world remains dangerously divided.
